title: Performance Characterization and Provenance of Distributed Task-based Workflows on HPC Platforms
problem: Task-based workflow management systems introduce unpredictable dynamicity that alters task execution order across runs, making performance characterization difficult in distributed HPC environments where resources are shared among multiple applications.
motivation: Understanding and reproducing the performance of task-based workflows is critical for optimizing resource utilization and debugging on large-scale HPC platforms.
method: The authors develop a layered characterization framework collecting data from three system levels: jobs, workflow management system (Dask.distributed), and operating system. They extend Dask.distributed with Mochi data services for high-fidelity task provenance capture and adapt the Darshan I/O characterization tool for detailed I/O metrics. Multi-layer data streams are combined and analyzed to provide performance insights and reproducibility assessment.
key_novelty: Integration of task provenance tracking with multi-level performance instrumentation (job, workflow, OS) for comprehensive characterization of Dask workflows on HPC systems.
contributions: Extension of Dask.distributed with Mochi data services for capturing high-fidelity task provenance
Adaptation of Darshan for gathering high-fidelity I/O data at workflow granularity
Framework for combining and processing multi-layer performance data to enable performance characterization and reproducibility analysis
primary_theme: Multi-layer performance and provenance characterization for distributed task workflows
